clue.text: Stop and take a meal at one of the estates

parts.note: to sup is to take supper, an evening meal
the press is called the fourth estate, after lords, clergy and commons

explanation.surface: Someone halts to have lunch on one of the big country estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estates' suggests landed property, but the press is the Fourth Estate of the realm.
explanation.definitionFit: To quash or hold something down is to bring it to a halt, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Remove vehicles overturned on junction

indicators.note: turned over in a down clue means the vehicles are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a cart and a bus are two vehicles
a T-junction gives the letter T

explanation.surface: Buses and carts have tipped over at a road junction, so clear them away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns both vehicles, giving SUB and TRAC (from BUS and CART) before T.
explanation.definitionFit: To take away a number or part is to deduct it, the arithmetic sense of removal.

clue.text: Charge for delivery when beer's on time

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A delivery fee is charged whenever the beer arrives on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts PORTER above AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The fee paid to a porter for carrying goods is the cost of having them carried and delivered.

clue.text: Legitimate male domain

parts.note: real means genuine or legitimate

explanation.surface: A rightful man's territory is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom or sphere of influence is a domain, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Man with pistol maybe to jump in front of the Queen

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above, in front of, the second

parts.note: to start is to jump with surprise
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A gunman is poised to leap ahead of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'man with pistol' sounds sinister but is the official firing the gun to begin a race.
explanation.definitionFit: At a race meeting the official who fires a pistol to send runners off is the person who begins the race.

clue.text: Behind craggy outcrop lurks a black beetle

indicators.note: behind tells us the next pieces come after the outcrop

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky outcrop on a hillside
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: A dark beetle hides behind a rugged rock.
explanation.walkthrough: A SCAR is a cliff or rocky bare patch, a northern English landscape word.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred beetle of ancient Egypt is a scarab, an example of the insect.

clue.text: Holed vessels — do they come ashore simultaneously?

parts.note: co- is a prefix meaning together or jointly
landers are those who land

explanation.surface: Perhaps boats with holes in them all reach the beach together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holed vessels' reads as leaky ships, but these are kitchen sieves.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen strainer is a bowl perforated with holes, so it is a vessel full of holes.

clue.text: Like some characters in rugby, not totally pleasant

parts.note: RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union

indicators.note: not totally means the word for pleasant loses its final letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Some players in a rugby side are not entirely agreeable people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' suggests people, but here they are letters of an alphabet; 'not totally' cuts NICE to NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes were letters of the old Germanic alphabet, so runic letters are such written symbols.

clue.text: One offering local deliveries?

parts.note: local is British slang for a neighbourhood pub, and this firm supplies the beer it pours

explanation.surface: A courier serves the nearby area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' as a noun is the British pub nearest your home.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer maker supplies ale to the pubs, the locals, that sell it.

clue.text: Cowboy to go collecting gold with companion

indicators.note: collecting means the word for go gathers the other pieces inside it

parts.note: the verb to go
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A ranch hand sets off to pick up gold along with a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American horseman herding cattle on the pampas is the local equivalent of a cowhand.

clue.text: Drill at army college in the country

annotationWithheld.why: Drill at army college in the country (5): BUR (a drill) + RMA (Royal Military Academy) gives BURRMA, one R too many; no parse found for BURMA
annotationWithheld.clue: Drill at army college in the country

clue.text: A label attached to weapon immediately

parts.note: a tag is a label
a lance is a long spear-like weapon

explanation.surface: A tag is tied onto a spear straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing something in one quick look means seeing it instantly, the idiom for immediacy.

clue.text: Using what's available in Bath, cure him, possibly

definitions.text: Using what's available in Bath, cure him, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals a rearrangement of the letters gathered
what lies within the word Bath, its inside letters without the ends

explanation.surface: A spa town's treatments might relieve a man's stiff joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the anagram. Bath is an English spa town long visited by sufferers of aching joints, so the whole clue also describes the patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Joint pain was the classic complaint sent to take the waters at Bath, so its patient is the stiff-jointed sufferer.

clue.text: Smooth iridescent substance from northern area

parts.note: an acre is a measure of area

explanation.surface: A glossy shimmering material comes from a region up north.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl, the shimmering lining of shells, is the substance meant.

clue.text: Cleaner going round distinguished member's room

indicators.note: going round means the cleaner's word encloses the other piece

parts.note: a char is a British cleaning woman
MBE is Member of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: The cleaning lady works her way around the room of an honoured club member.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR (charwoman) is an old British word for a hired cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is an old or formal word for a room, especially a bedroom.

clue.text: Like big hall's bar with inlaid quartz.

indicators.note: with inlaid means the second piece is set into the first

parts.note: to ban is to bar
quartz is a crystalline form of silica

explanation.surface: A great hall's bar counter is decorated with set-in crystal.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica was a large Roman hall, so the adjective describes something resembling one.

clue.text: Confer about rough seas in port

indicators.note: about means the word for confer is turned round

parts.note: to do someone an honour is to confer it

indicators.note: rough signals that the letters of seas are churned up

explanation.surface: People discuss stormy waters at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns DO into OD, and 'rough' rearranges SEAS as ESSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port city in Ukraine.

clue.text: A garment that's out of this world?

definitions.text: A garment that's out of this world?

parts.words: A garment that's out of this world?
parts.note: out of this world usually means superb, but read literally it means worn beyond Earth by astronauts

explanation.surface: A fabulous piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts wear a pressurised outfit when working beyond the atmosphere.

clue.text: City criminal stifles exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: stifles means the criminal's word smothers another piece inside it

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods
lor is a dialect exclamation of surprise, from Lord

explanation.surface: A city villain muffles a startled cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the Italian city of Tuscany, an example of a city.

clue.text: What smoke comes from, they say, or what detects it?

indicators.note: they say signals a word that is pronounced like another

parts.note: a censer is a vessel that burns incense, so smoke rises from it

explanation.surface: A riddle about the source of smoke and the device that notices it.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoke alarm's detector is a device that perceives a physical signal.

clue.text: Deodorant I can't wait for … !

definitions.meaning: a deodorant applied with a rolling ball
an exclamation of eagerness, as in come quickly, the weekend

explanation.definitionFit: A ball applicator type of antiperspirant, and the idiom urging a longed-for time to arrive.

clue.text: Complain about twerp's drinking-bout

indicators.note: about means the complaint word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to wail is to complain loudly
an ass is a fool or twerp

explanation.surface: Someone moans about a fool's drinking session.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassail is a festive toast and the bout of merry drinking around it.

clue.text: Driver lost in the course of hostilities

indicators.note: in the course of means one piece runs inside the other

parts.note: war means hostilities
gone means lost

explanation.surface: A driver went missing during the fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon driver drives a horse-drawn cart, a dated job title.

clue.text: Sign walker spotted, mile from the start

indicators.note: from the start means the letter for mile is removed at the beginning

parts.note: a marcher is someone walking in a march

explanation.surface: A walker noticed a signpost a mile from the starting point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' means a sign of the zodiac: Sagittarius is depicted as a bowman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagittarius, a zodiac sign, is pictured as a bowman with drawn bow.

clue.text: Splendid drink for knocking back

indicators.note: knocking back reads as drinking down, but here it turns the word round

parts.note: lager is a drink

explanation.surface: A fine drink fit to be downed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' is slang for drinking, but here it reverses LAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something royal and majestic is magnificent, a synonym of splendid.

clue.text: Dance girl needing musical work

parts.note: gal is a girl
op, opus, is a numbered musical work

explanation.surface: A girl wants some music to dance to.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively 19th-century ballroom dance in 2/4 time, an example of a dance.

clue.text: Ray's annual journey

parts.note: how far a beam travels in twelve months, read as a unit of distance

explanation.surface: Someone called Ray makes a trip each year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name but is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of astronomical distance is how far light goes in a year.

clue.text: As a misanthrope, I'm not mixing

indicators.note: mixing signals that the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A man-hater refuses to socialise.
explanation.walkthrough: Timon of Athens is Shakespeare's famous hater of mankind.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Athenian who turns against humanity is the archetypal hater of mankind.

clue.text: What Orange king had for money?

definitions.text: What Orange king had for money?

parts.words: What Orange king had for money?
parts.note: William of Orange ruled jointly with Mary, so he held a share of the throne; also an old British coin

explanation.surface: A question about a Dutch monarch's cash.
explanation.walkthrough: William III of Orange reigned jointly with Mary II; the coin was a British piece worth two shillings and sixpence before 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: An old British coin worth two and sixpence, punning on a shared throne.

clue.text: Grieve a little while by the ashes?

parts.note: mo is short for moment
the Ashes, England v Australia cricket's trophy, is a tiny urn

explanation.surface: Someone mourns briefly beside a loved one's remains.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the Test cricket series between England and Australia, its trophy a small urn.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament or feel sorrow for a loss is the same as grieving.

clue.text: Robbery in a wood on the far side of river

indicators.note: on the far side of puts the following pieces after the river letter

parts.note: pine is a wood

explanation.surface: A theft takes place in a forest across the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapine is plunder and seizure of property by force, a literary word for robbery.

clue.text: It's not fair when beast circumvents trap

indicators.note: circumvents means the beast's word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a brute is a beast
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A monster gets round a snare, which is unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fair' sounds like a complaint of injustice; it means not fair-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark-haired person is literally not blonde or light-haired.
